sourceReference.title: docs(arch): ratify responsibility, visibility and dependency contracts (#636)

ac3Rationale: ARH1 changes contract bytes only: no state, query, map, cache or scheduling boundary is touched at this node, so fresh-versus-incremental equivalence, edit/revert, cancellation, stale/partial rejection and deterministic ordering remain owned and proven by their untouched owners (rev11.scheduler-runtime admission and cancellation, rev11.flow dispatch, B4R0 source lineage, LSO0 snapshot publication). The state-lifetime rows below name those owners so the heirs (ARH3/ARH4) inherit the obligations instead of re-deriving them.

ac4Obligations.obligation: document the per-hotspot import direction, constructor capabilities, state lifetimes and minimal public surfaces in the architecture/contributor documentation, including the VIM/DX capability mapping for each retained surface and the exact host/profile evidence every measured population was taken on; the contract rows are the source of truth, the docs are delivery.

enforce layerRules mayImport/mustNotImport and the module surfaceDeclarations (including the pub(crate) boundaries) as targeted compile-time visibility/dependency checks in existing tooling; no second status system.

characterize current surfaces before any narrowing lands and re-derive the ARH0 inventory populations and this node's importer/consumer populations on the then-current candidate (the importer and consumer populations are live set joins the verifier derives from the measured tree on every run; file size and item counts are not recorded); record any drift in host/profile basis alongside the re-derived populations.
any examples/reference addition that consumes these hotspots uses only the retained public surfaces listed here (DOC1-tested examples stay inside the contract).

the semantic_query narrowing lands together with the recorded migration notes: the 299 consumer files on the bulk row move to the test-support re-export surface or a retained session-facing surface in the same change, and the 11 retained assoc items stay pub for the ffi/napi/wasm production consumers and the verter_session files that import only retained types; no unrecorded consumer may appear between ratification and the narrowing.

the scheduler field and test-hook narrowings land together with their recorded per-hook consumer migrations (same-change, per the cutover register dispositions); the exact-consumer invariant is re-derived on the executing candidate so no unrecorded consumer breaks.

ac5Rationale: No new latency, work, allocation or RSS budget is created or measured at this node; the ratified performance methodology is untouched. Visibility narrowing (pub -> pub(crate), test hooks to test configuration) shrinks compile surfaces only via the heirs and is not claimed as a performance win. No obsolete path is retired here: ARH1 supersedes nothing with a second authority, so there is no capability to narrow in-tree at this node.

layerRules.rule: scheduler-runtime stays below every orchestration crate: it may depend only on the leaf utility crates
layerRules.evidence: crates/verter_scheduler/Cargo.toml [dependencies] is exactly audit/debug_assert/language/span; scheduler.rs imports verter_language and verter_audit only

layerRules.rule: the semantic core never depends upward on orchestration or transport
layerRules.evidence: crates/verter_semantic/Cargo.toml [dependencies]; the verter_session:: mentions inside verter_semantic sources are doc comments, not imports
layerRules.nonHotspotRationale: verter_semantic owns no ARH1 hotspot, but it is the semantic substrate under the semantic_query and flow-dispatch authorities (the FunctionFlowGraph and FlowSliceIR state owners live here); its layer rule is ratified in this constitution so the semantic core stays governed below orchestration until a semantic-core node owns it

layerRules.rule: editor/transport/FFI crates are leaves: the session core never imports them (they import the session)
layerRules.nonHotspotRationale: verter_session owns no ARH1 hotspot: the semantic type engine (semantic_query, the project semantic dispatch and its flow-return and build modules) lives in verter_type_engine; the session is the host orchestration layer above that engine, and its layer rule is ratified so the editor/transport/FFI leaves stay out of its dependencies

layerRules.rule: module-resolution implementation consumes query-boundary inputs and parser-free leaves, never host orchestration or syntax frontends
layerRules.evidence: crates/verter_resolution/Cargo.toml production dependencies and crate-private ResolverObservation seal
layerRules.nonHotspotRationale: The reusable workspace module-resolution implementation is a cohesive kernel below workspace/session consumers; supplied values remain in the query boundary.

layerRules.rule: source-side declaration and flow lowering consumes the syntax front-end and the query boundary only, never the type engine or host orchestration

the semantic type engine consumes the shared query vocabulary, the execution substrate and parser-free leaves only, never a parser, the compiler, the session, the workspace, source lowering, module resolution, the concrete scheduler, the protocol or a provider

authority.evidence: dag.rs module contract: SchedulerDag is the SOLE readiness authority; all admission, dedup, generation supersession, dependency gating, blocker resolution and capacity accounting flow through it
driver.rs module contract: the driver owns all admission and ordering policy and drains the SubmissionInbox
cancellation.rs module contract: one-shot clonable cancellation latches; dropping a handle cancels its still-pending work

allowedImportDirection.ownerCratePopulation: the importers array is the complete cross-crate population (48 files: 26 verter_session src files, 17 verter_session integration tests, three verter_lsp audit test cases, verter_dx_baseline materialize and verter_napi lib), enforced by the verifier in both directions on comment-stripped syntax; crates/verter_lsp/src/external_ts_sync.rs references verter_execution::cancellation, not the scheduler module, and is deliberately absent; population re-derivation on a moving candidate is ARH2's recorded obligation
allowedImportDirection.measurementBasis: production import tree: cfg(test) and cfg(all(test, ..)) items are stripped before measuring and BOTH use statements and inline crate paths in code position (verter_audit::attribute! macros, crossbeam_channel::Sender parameter types, the feature-gated hotpath::wrap alias, and crate::module::Item paths like crate::cache_id::SchedulerCacheId fields, crate::execution::pool::SchedulerCpuPool constructor parameters, crate::request_context::RequestContext, crate::audit_publish, crate::dedupe_hook, crate::execution::owner_command and crate::source_root references) are measured, so the declared sets equal the production direction both ways; verter_audit is measured through the module root's production re-export and its inline attribute! paths; cache_id and request_context are production crate-internal roots measured through inline paths (their use-statement imports are test configuration), and execution is the declared crate-internal root for the moved execution adapters (pool, owner_command, executor, host_cpu_pool, cpu_concurrency), measured through both its production use statements and its inline crate::execution:: paths

rules: pools and the source loader are host-injected Arc handles: the scheduler constructs no pool and performs no file I/O in the constructor
spawns exactly one driver thread on native targets and none on wasm32
no parse, analysis, compile or semantic work happens at construction time
the stage executor is injected: DefaultExecutor is chosen by the caller, never constructed here to reach semantic crates
same pool-injection and single-driver-thread capability as new
synchronous-driver variant of new with the same injected-pool capability; wasm32 target carries no native pool parameter
synchronous-driver variant of with_executor with the same injected-executor capability

stateLifetimes.evidence: per-file CURRENT snapshots only; a generation bump makes the prior source immediately unreachable
epoch-indexed MVCC source authority; consumers capture an O(1) SchedulerSourceRoot and read the world as of that capture
single driver-owned readiness authority; lock rank dag > source-root publication > nodes shard
lock-free submission inbox drained by the driver loop

deferred blocker ids are replayed at Source completion; no generation-floor history exists: external artifact publication and cleanup are fenced by the scheduler-minted SourceWitness, and host revisions and version rails name the committing node incarnation through SourceVersion

teardown pair driven by quiesce/restart_driver
one-shot latches riding work items; the owning handle trips the token on Drop

ac4Rationale: AC4 surfaces a contract-only node cannot discharge with artifacts are specified for its producers instead: the VIM/DX capability mapping and the exact host/profile evidence are DOC2/ARH2 obligations above; migration notes are each narrowing row's exact consumersAffected inventory plus the cutover dispositions; permissions are not applicable (no capability, filesystem, network or editor-permission surface is created or widened at this node, so there is no permission note to publish); uncertainty is recorded as importer and consumer populations joined by the verifier against the live tree on every run (no file size or item count is recorded), with the source title and date retained as descriptive context only, and no partial or conditional runtime result is claimed anywhere in these bytes.
